Durruti Column.fact: On 4 September 1936, the Republicans again attempted to capture Sietemo, but the Nationalists had reinforced their positions with another infantry company, a Falangist detachment and many more Civil Guards, and placed 6 machine guns and an artillery battery on the town's high ground. After three days, the Republican militias captured the outskirts of the town and began house-to-house fighting against the Nationalists.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Nationalists retreated down the _____ road, and dug in behind the Flumen river
Durruti Column.fact: The Nationalists retreated down the Estrecho Quinto road, and dug in behind the Flumen river.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The offensive immediately continued on from _____
Durruti Column.fact: With Sietemo captured, the Durruti Column seized 2 artillery cannons, 4 mortar cannons, 8 machine guns and 300 rifles; they also took 150 Nationalists as prisoners of war. The offensive immediately continued on from Sietemo.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: From 15 to 18 _____, the Republican militias attempted to flank the Nationalist lines, but faced heavy resistance
Durruti Column.fact: From 15 to 18 September, the Republican militias attempted to flank the Nationalist lines, but faced heavy resistance. On 30 September, the Durruti Column captured Loporzano; the Republican forces also captured Forniellos and placed Tierz under siege.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Nationalists then withdrew to Huesca city, leaving the _____ way forward undefended
Durruti Column.fact: From 15 to 18 September, the Republican militias attempted to flank the Nationalist lines, but faced heavy resistance. On 30 September, the Durruti Column captured Loporzano; the Republican forces also captured Forniellos and placed Tierz under siege.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: After the _____ victory on the Huesca front, Durruti gave a speech calling for all weapons still being held in the rearguard to be sent to the frontlines
Durruti Column.fact: The Nationalists then withdrew to Huesca city, leaving the Republican way forward undefended. After the Republican victory on the Huesca front, Durruti gave a speech calling for all weapons still being held in the rearguard to be sent to the frontlines.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: This caused fierce debates to break out between the _____ of Catalonia (PSUC) and the Barcelona revolutionary committees, as the former denounced the latter for continuing to hold on to their weapons
Durruti Column.fact: This caused fierce debates to break out between the Unified Socialist Party of Catalonia (PSUC) and the Barcelona revolutionary committees, as the former denounced the latter for continuing to hold on to their weapons.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The debate came to a head when workers discovered the PSUC had themselves stockpiled weapons, taken from the _____, in their offices in Sabadell
Durruti Column.fact: The debate came to a head when workers discovered the PSUC had themselves stockpiled weapons, taken from the Karl Marx Barracks, in their offices in Sabadell. Diego Abad de Santillán ordered the Karl Marx Barracks to hand the weapons over, telling them that they risked an armed response if they failed to do so; the 8 machine guns which the PSUC had stockpiled in Sabadell were quickly given up.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Column captured many prisoners of war, largely from the ranks of the _____ and Carlists, and a number of Nationalists even defected to their side
Durruti Column.fact: The Column captured many prisoners of war, largely from the ranks of the Falangists and Carlists, and a number of Nationalists even defected to their side.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The meeting also resolved to establish a single _____, which would direct the military effort on the front line
Durruti Column.fact: The meeting also resolved to establish a single War Committee, which would direct the military effort on the front line. In establishing the War Committee, the Regional Defense Council sought to resolve the problems ca.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: These internal conflicts prevented the militia columns from organising an offensive on _____
Durruti Column.fact: These internal conflicts prevented the militia columns from organising an offensive on Huesca.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Representatives of the various columns gathered together in Sarinyena, where the new _____ was established, despite PSUC objections
Durruti Column.fact: Representatives of the various columns gathered together in Sarinyena, where the new War Committee was established, despite PSUC objections.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: By this time, Felipe Díaz _____ had been appointed as the Catalan Minister of Defense by the reorganised Catalan government
Durruti Column.fact: By this time, Felipe Díaz Sandino had been appointed as the Catalan Minister of Defense by the reorganised Catalan government. On 8 October, while the Durruti Column was still under Nationalist fire, Díaz Sandino called for all militia columns to meet in Sarinyena to discuss the formation of a general staff.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The meeting was attended by representatives of both the _____ and CNT columns, forcing them to directly confront the dispute between them
Durruti Column.fact: The meeting was attended by representatives of both the PSUC and CNT columns, forcing them to directly confront the dispute between them. José del Barrio of the PSUC objected to the proposal due to the ongoing political conflict between the PSUC and CNT, but Díaz Sandino repeated his appeal for unity as he believed it was the only way to beat back the Nationalists.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: After days of heavy fighting, the _____ captured Lecinyena and killed many of its Republican defenders
Durruti Column.fact: José del Barrio of the PSUC objected to the proposal due to the ongoing political conflict between the PSUC and CNT, but Díaz Sandino repeated his appeal for unity as he believed it was the only way to beat back the Nationalists. After days of heavy fighting, the Nationalists captured Lecinyena and killed many of its Republican defenders.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: With the _____ supply lines disrupted by the capture of Licenyena, on 12 October, the Nationalists attacked POUM-held positions north of the Sierra d'Alcubierre
Durruti Column.fact: After days of heavy fighting, the Nationalists captured Lecinyena and killed many of its Republican defenders. With the Republican supply lines disrupted by the capture of Licenyena, on 12 October, the Nationalists attacked POUM-held positions north of the Sierra d'Alcubierre.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The International Group, which consisted of 40 men led by _____, broke off from the rest of the Column and went towards Perdiguera
Durruti Column.fact: The International Group, which consisted of 40 men led by Louis Berthomieu, broke off from the rest of the Column and went towards Perdiguera.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: There they attacked the _____ defenses with hand grenades, entered the town and finally defeated the local garrison on 16 October
Durruti Column.fact: The Durruti Column provided reinforcements and contained the Nationalists at Alcubierre, before mustering their forces for a counterattack against Licenyena. There they attacked the Nationalists defenses with hand grenades, entered the town and finally defeated the local garrison on 16 October.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Nationalists were quickly reinforced by two battalions from _____, which besieged Perdiguera
Durruti Column.fact: The Nationalists were quickly reinforced by two battalions from Zaragoza, which besieged Perdiguera.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: When the _____ retook Perdiguera, they executed three foreign nurses from the Red Cross
Durruti Column.fact: The Durruti Column attempted to counterattack and aid the besieged International Group, but a surprise attack by another detachment of Nationalists prevented them from doing so. When the Nationalists retook Perdiguera, they executed three foreign nurses from the Red Cross.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: One Belgian member of the Column, _____, reported that "the territory gained didn't compensate for the Column's losses
Durruti Column.fact: One Belgian member of the Column, Mathieu Corman, reported that "the territory gained didn't compensate for the Column's losses.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: While the reorganisation took place, the Column received a visit from a CNT delegation, which requested one of its members be sent to Moscow for an upcoming anniversary celebration of the _____
Durruti Column.fact: While the reorganisation took place, the Column received a visit from a CNT delegation, which requested one of its members be sent to Moscow for an upcoming anniversary celebration of the October Revolution.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Durruti drafted a greeting to _____ workers, but Carreño was not able to read the statement publicly in Moscow
Durruti Column.fact: Durruti drafted a greeting to Russian workers, but Carreño was not able to read the statement publicly in Moscow.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Column was then visited by _____, the General Secretary of the CNT, who requested that they be transferred from the Aragon front to Castile
Durruti Column.fact: The Column was then visited by Horacio Prieto, the General Secretary of the CNT, who requested that they be transferred from the Aragon front to Castile.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: José Miaja was left in command of the city's defence, with _____ as his chief of staff, while the people of the city rallied to defend their neighbourhoods from the advancing Nationalists
Durruti Column.fact: José Miaja was left in command of the city's defence, with Vicente Rojo as his chief of staff, while the people of the city rallied to defend their neighbourhoods from the advancing Nationalists.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Republican government also sent _____ to secure an agreement for the Column's presence
Durruti Column.fact: The Republican government also sent Federica Montseny to secure an agreement for the Column's presence.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: With promises from _____ that the Soviets would arm any reinforcements which were sent to Madrid, on 11 November, Diego Abad de Santillán called a meeting of the militia columns in Aragon
Durruti Column.fact: With promises from Ovseenko that the Soviets would arm any reinforcements which were sent to Madrid, on 11 November, Diego Abad de Santillán called a meeting of the militia columns in Aragon.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: There they decided that Durruti would lead his Column to the _____ front, for which they planned to recruit 12,000 militiamen
Durruti Column.fact: With Madrid under siege, on 9 November, the central section of the CNT dispatched David Antona to Burcharaloz to request the Durruti Column be transferred to the capital. With promises from Ovseenko that the Soviets would arm any reinforcements which were sent to Madrid, on 11 November, Diego Abad de Santillán called a meeting of the militia columns in Aragon.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: On 13 _____, the militiamen bound for Madrid went to the port of Barcelona, unloaded boxes of weapon shipments from Mexico and loaded them onto train carriages
Durruti Column.fact: On 13 November, the militiamen bound for Madrid went to the port of Barcelona, unloaded boxes of weapon shipments from Mexico and loaded them onto train carriages.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: By the time they left _____ by train, they had not slept in 48 hours
Durruti Column.fact: On 13 November, the militiamen bound for Madrid went to the port of Barcelona, unloaded boxes of weapon shipments from Mexico and loaded them onto train carriages. By the time they left Barcelona by train, they had not slept in 48 hours.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: That night, the train left _____ in the direction of Valencia
Durruti Column.fact: On 13 November, the militiamen bound for Madrid went to the port of Barcelona, unloaded boxes of weapon shipments from Mexico and loaded them onto train carriages. By the time they left Barcelona by train, they had not slept in 48 hours.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: They later discovered that the weapons - Winchester Model _____ rifles - were fragile, often jammed and did not take ammunition of the Spanish caliber
Durruti Column.fact: They later discovered that the weapons - Winchester Model 1886 rifles - were fragile, often jammed and did not take ammunition of the Spanish caliber.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The following day, they were transferred onto buses and trucks, as the _____ had destroyed rail lines between Valencia and Madrid
Durruti Column.fact: The following day, they were transferred onto buses and trucks, as the Nationalists had destroyed rail lines between Valencia and Madrid.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Durruti's biographer _____ disputes whether Mamsurov ever advised the Column
Durruti Column.fact: Durruti's biographer Abel Paz estimated that the Column initially consisted of 2,000 militiamen, although Diego Abad de Santillán put the number at 3,000, Joan Garcia Oliver put it at as many 5,000 and Soviet journalist Mikhail Koltsov put it as few as 1,200.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: In interviews with _____, José Mira, Antonio Mora, Ricardo Rionda, Liberto Ros, none of them supported the claim that Mamsurov had been the Column's military advisor
Durruti Column.fact: In interviews with Antonio Bonilla, José Mira, Antonio Mora, Ricardo Rionda, Liberto Ros, none of them supported the claim that Mamsurov had been the Column's military advisor.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Durruti was also given command over the López _____, which he ordered to attack the Nationalists at the Casa de Campo
Durruti Column.fact: Durruti was also given command over the López Tienda Column, which he ordered to attack the Nationalists at the Casa de Campo.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: It was the first militia column established in _____ after the defeat of the July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona
Durruti Column.fact: It was the first militia column set up in Revolutionary Catalonia after the defeat of the July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: By mid-1937, it was reorganised into 26th Division of the _____, which continued fighting until the very end of the war
Durruti Column.fact: By mid-1937, it was reorganised into 26th Division of the Spanish Republican Army, which continued fighting until the very end of the war.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: This version of events was taken up by historians such as Robert Garland Colodny, Pierre Broué and _____, who each in turn misidentified the López-Tienda Column as the Durruti Column
Durruti Column.fact: This version of events was taken up by historians such as Robert Garland Colodny, Pierre Broué and Hugh Thomas, who each in turn misidentified the López-Tienda Column as the Durruti Column.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Column captured several towns in the east of Zaragoza province, but was halted _____ outside the city and forced to wait for reinforcements
Durruti Column.fact: The Column captured several towns in the east of Zaragoza province, but was halted 20 kilometers outside the city and forced to wait for reinforcements.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Column was halted by enemy lines roughly _____ outside of Zaragoza, where they then dug trenches and set up machine gun posts
Durruti Column.fact: The Column was halted by enemy lines roughly 20 kilometers outside of Zaragoza, where they then dug trenches and set up machine gun posts.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: By the end of the day, the Durruti Column had regained control of the area and drove the Nationalists back _____ towards Perdiguera
Durruti Column.fact: By the end of the day, the Durruti Column had regained control of the area and drove the Nationalists back 15 kilometers towards Perdiguera.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: On the morning of 15 _____, Vicente Rojo ordered a counteroffensive along the Manzanres to push the Nationalists back over the Franceses Bridge, which would prevent them from entering Madrid
Durruti Column.fact: On the morning of 15 November, Vicente Rojo ordered a counteroffensive along the Manzanres to push the Nationalists back over the Franceses Bridge, which would prevent them from entering Madrid.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: While two tanks and a _____ detachment were crossing the bridge, the Republicans blew it up with dynamite
Durruti Column.fact: While two tanks and a Moroccan detachment were crossing the bridge, the Republicans blew it up with dynamite.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At 09:00 on 15 _____, they crossed into Madrid
Durruti Column.fact: At 09:00 on 15 November, they crossed into Madrid.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: As they passed the _____, they were attacked by the Nationalists inside; the Column stormed the embassy and seized its arsenal of machine guns and grenades
Durruti Column.fact: As they passed the Finnish Embassy, they were attacked by the Nationalists inside; the Column stormed the embassy and seized its arsenal of machine guns and grenades.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: They then stopped at a primary school on Calle de _____, where they were given accommodation
Durruti Column.fact: They then stopped at a primary school on Calle de Hortaleza, where they were given accommodation.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At 16:00, _____ arrived at their door and told them that the Nationalists had advanced to Avenida de los Rosales and requested they go there immediately to push them back
Durruti Column.fact: At 16:00, Federica Montseny arrived at their door and told them that the Nationalists had advanced to Avenida de los Rosales and requested they go there immediately to push them back.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Shortly after _____ left, Durruti arrived and told them that they had been assigned a new position
Durruti Column.fact: At 16:00, Federica Montseny arrived at their door and told them that the Nationalists had advanced to Avenida de los Rosales and requested they go there immediately to push them back. Shortly after Montseny left, Durruti arrived and told them that they had been assigned a new position.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Nationalists had captured part of the _____, so they went to the front at 02:00 on 16 November
Durruti Column.fact: The Nationalists had captured part of the University City, so they went to the front at 02:00 on 16 November.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: When they arrived at the Cárcel Modelo, Durruti and _____ told them which positions they would occupy
Durruti Column.fact: When they arrived at the Cárcel Modelo, Durruti and Manzana told them which positions they would occupy.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At the onset of the _____ of Ciudad Universitaria, all the Republican reserves were transferred to the area for a counterattack
Durruti Column.fact: At the onset of the Battle of Ciudad Universitaria, all the Republican reserves were transferred to the area for a counterattack.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Following hours of fighting, including some close-quarters combat, by 07:00, the Column captured the _____ and the asylum
Durruti Column.fact: The Column's right flank, led by Liberto Roig, advanced through the Parque del Oeste and occupied the Rubio Institute; its left flank, led by José Mira, was to occupy the Santa Cristina Asylum, the Hospital Clinic, the Casa de Velázquez and the Faculty of Philology, where they would reestablish contact with the XI Brigade. Following hours of fighting, including some close-quarters combat, by 07:00, the Column captured the Hospital Clinic and the asylum.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At 09:00, the _____ counterattacked with artillery, tanks and aerial bombardments; some Nationalist planes were shot down and crashed on the Column's lines
Durruti Column.fact: At 09:00, the Nationalists counterattacked with artillery, tanks and aerial bombardments; some Nationalist planes were shot down and crashed on the Column's lines.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Having already suffered heavy casualties, the Column was preoccupied with rescuing the wounded and failed to take the _____ de Velázquez
Durruti Column.fact: The Column's right flank, led by Liberto Roig, advanced through the Parque del Oeste and occupied the Rubio Institute; its left flank, led by José Mira, was to occupy the Santa Cristina Asylum, the Hospital Clinic, the Casa de Velázquez and the Faculty of Philology, where they would reestablish contact with the XI Brigade. Having already suffered heavy casualties, the Column was preoccupied with rescuing the wounded and failed to take the Casa de Velázquez.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: After hours of fighting, they finally received reinforcements from the _____ at 11:00
Durruti Column.fact: After hours of fighting, they finally received reinforcements from the Fifth Regiment at 11:00.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Well into the following night, they continued fighting to capture the Casa de Velázquez and the _____ of Philology
Durruti Column.fact: Well into the following night, they continued fighting to capture the Casa de Velázquez and the Faculty of Philology. Together with the international volunteers, the Column managed to capture the Faculty of Philology, despite constant Nationalist attacks, by the time the sun rose on 17 November.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Together with the international volunteers, the Column managed to capture the _____ of Philology, despite constant Nationalist attacks, by the time the sun rose on 17 November
Durruti Column.fact: Well into the following night, they continued fighting to capture the Casa de Velázquez and the Faculty of Philology. Together with the international volunteers, the Column managed to capture the Faculty of Philology, despite constant Nationalist attacks, by the time the sun rose on 17 November.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At 23:00, the Column finally managed to link up with the XI _____
Durruti Column.fact: At 23:00, the Column finally managed to link up with the XI Brigade.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Members of the _____ attempted to desert the Hospital Clinic, but a group led by Miguel Yoldi prevented them from fleeing
Durruti Column.fact: Members of the Fifth Regiment attempted to desert the Hospital Clinic, but a group led by Miguel Yoldi prevented them from fleeing.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: That night was marked by continuous waves of bayonet charges from the _____, who the Column met with machine gun fire
Durruti Column.fact: That night was marked by continuous waves of bayonet charges from the Nationalists, who the Column met with machine gun fire.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Durruti attempted to seek replacements from _____, the leader of the CNT's Madrid Defense Committee
Durruti Column.fact: Durruti attempted to seek replacements from Eduardo Val, the leader of the CNT's Madrid Defense Committee.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Val was able to replace Yoldi, but _____ insisted on fighting, despite being wounded
Durruti Column.fact: Val was able to replace Yoldi, but Manzana insisted on fighting, despite being wounded.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Liberto Roig then informed Durruti that José _____ had been wounded and that the Column was insisting on relief
Durruti Column.fact: Liberto Roig then informed Durruti that José Mira had been wounded and that the Column was insisting on relief. He also promised that he would replace Mira later that night.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: He also promised that he would replace _____ later that night
Durruti Column.fact: Liberto Roig then informed Durruti that José Mira had been wounded and that the Column was insisting on relief. He also promised that he would replace Mira later that night.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: They believed that the _____ had exhausted themselves attempting to take Madrid, and that if they could hold out another 24 hours, then the battle for Ciudad Universitaria would be won
Durruti Column.fact: They believed that the Nationalists had exhausted themselves attempting to take Madrid, and that if they could hold out another 24 hours, then the battle for Ciudad Universitaria would be won.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: When Durruti returned to the front, the Column held the front line from the Directorate-General of the Civil Guard to the _____
Durruti Column.fact: When Durruti returned to the front, the Column held the front line from the Directorate-General of the Civil Guard to the Thermal Power Plant.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: By 18 November, the _____ had fallen under Nationalist control
Durruti Column.fact: By 18 November, the Hospital Clinic had fallen under Nationalist control. At 04:00 on 19 November, the Durruti Column fired a volley at the Hospital Clinic, and when there was no return fire, a group of militiamen moved.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: To recapture it, the Durruti Column first took an adjacent block of houses on Avenida de Pablo Iglesias, which was _____ away from the Hospital
Durruti Column.fact: To recapture it, the Durruti Column first took an adjacent block of houses on Avenida de Pablo Iglesias, which was 400 metres away from the Hospital.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: That day, a member of the _____ pointed out that the Nationalists left the building each night and returned in the morning, and proposed they take it at night
Durruti Column.fact: That day, a member of the Rosal Column pointed out that the Nationalists left the building each night and returned in the morning, and proposed they take it at night.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The offensive against the _____ began at 06:00, in heavy torrential rain
Durruti Column.fact: At 04:00 on 19 November, the Durruti Column fired a volley at the Hospital Clinic, and when there was no return fire, a group of militiamen moved to occupy the building. The offensive against the Hospital Clinic began at 06:00, in heavy torrential rain.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The Column was attacked by _____ on the lower floors, so they retreated to the building's upper floors and roofs
Durruti Column.fact: That day, a member of the Rosal Column pointed out that the Nationalists left the building each night and returned in the morning, and proposed they take it at night. The Column was attacked by Nationalists on the lower floors, so they retreated to the building's upper floors and roofs.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Meanwhile, the Column had also sustained heavy casualties at the Palace of Moncloa and the _____, forcing them to change locations
Durruti Column.fact: Meanwhile, the Column had also sustained heavy casualties at the Palace of Moncloa and the Model Prison, forcing them to change locations.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The two reserve companies withdrew from the _____ only hours after they were deployed
Durruti Column.fact: The two reserve companies withdrew from the Hospital Clinic only hours after they were deployed. As the situation at the Hospital Clinic continued to deteriorate, Durruti decided to visit the front personally.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: As the situation at the _____ continued to deteriorate, Durruti decided to visit the front personally
Durruti Column.fact: The two reserve companies withdrew from the Hospital Clinic only hours after they were deployed. As the situation at the Hospital Clinic continued to deteriorate, Durruti decided to visit the front personally.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: At 12:30, _____ sent a message to Durruti, begging for relief, as the Column had suffered heavy casualties and had not slept or eaten in days
Durruti Column.fact: At 12:30, Mira sent a message to Durruti, begging for relief, as the Column had suffered heavy casualties and had not slept or eaten in days.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Inspired by their fallen leader, the Column continued to defend _____
Durruti Column.fact: Inspired by their fallen leader, the Column continued to defend Madrid. Anarchist historiography attributes the Republican victory in the battle of Madrid to the Durruti Column.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Meanwhile, _____ Vázquez, the new General Secretary of the CNT, began considering who to replace Durruti at the head of the Column
Durruti Column.fact: Meanwhile, Mariano R. Vázquez, the new General Secretary of the CNT, began considering who to replace Durruti at the head of the Column.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: They ultimately decided to send Sanz to Madrid to take over the Column, and transferred _____ back to the Aragon front to lead its forces there
Durruti Column.fact: They ultimately decided to send Sanz to Madrid to take over the Column, and transferred Manzana back to the Aragon front to lead its forces there.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: The militiamen told Sanz that they believed Durruti had been killed by "our enemies within the _____" and warned him that he might also be in danger
Durruti Column.fact: The militiamen told Sanz that they believed Durruti had been killed by "our enemies within the Republic" and warned him that he might also be in danger.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Soviet journalist _____ believed that the only people capable of killing Durruti were the "adventurist members" of his own Column
Durruti Column.fact: Soviet journalist Roman Karmen believed that the only people capable of killing Durruti were the "adventurist members" of his own Column.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: French historians _____é and Émile Temime later repeated this version of events, speculating that one of the Column's militiamen had resented Durruti's strict discipline
Durruti Column.fact: This version of events was taken up by historians such as Robert Garland Colodny, Pierre Broué and Hugh Thomas, who each in turn misidentified the López-Tienda Column as the Durruti Column. According to Robert J. Alexander, 1,400 of the Column's militiamen had ultimately been transferred; Michael Alpert and Antony Beevor said Durruti had brought 3,000 men with him; and French historians Pierre Broué and Émile Temime put the number as high as 3,500.

Durruti Column.subject: Indian Languages
Durruti Column.question: Spanish historian _____ took offense to the Stalinist narrative, describing it as "the greatest possible affront" to the Columnists who had followed Durruti to Madrid and died in the fighting there

Ephesian Tale.question: The governor views this as a miracle and has _____ imprisoned but well cared for until he can tell his story

Ephesian Tale.question: The governor helps him sail to _____ to continue his search, and has Cyno crucified in his place

Fidelis of Sigmaringen.subject: Indian Languages
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.question: He was buried by _____ the next day
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.fact: He was buried by Catholics the next day.

Fidelis of Sigmaringen.subject: Indian Languages
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.question: The Protestant minister who had participated in Fidelis' martyrdom was converted by this circumstance, made a public abjuration of _____ and was received into the Catholic Church
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.fact: The Protestant minister who had participated in Fidelis' martyrdom was converted by this circumstance, made a public abjuration of Calvinism and was received into the Catholic Church.

Fidelis of Sigmaringen.question: Fidelis and his companions entered into Prättigau, a small district of Graubünden, in 1622, on the Feast of the _____, January 6
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.fact: Fidelis and his companions entered into Prättigau, a small district of Graubünden, in 1622, on the Feast of the Epiphany, January 6.

Fidelis of Sigmaringen.question: On 24 _____ 1622, Fidelis made his confession, celebrated Mass and then preached at Grüsch
Fidelis of Sigmaringen.fact: On 24 April 1622, Fidelis made his confession, celebrated Mass and then preached at Grüsch.
